Include realistic 3D graphics, third-person camera, smooth character movement, flashlight, rain, fog, terrifying monsters, fictional weapons, limited ammunition, inventory, health, puzzles, locked doors, exploration, cinematic cutscenes, atmospheric sound, save system and mobile controls if supported.

Create detailed environments, intelligent enemies, memorable encounters and a mysterious storyline. Make every mission playable, every interaction functional and all chapters connected.

Future ending: The complete 12-chapter campaign will culminate in Arjun discovering the truth about Project Eclipse and making a final decision that determines one of three endings: sacrifice, escape or uncovering the hidden organisation behind the experiment.

Prioritise beautiful graphics, immersive horror, stable gameplay and a polished experience. Do not create a simple shooting demo. Build a complete playable Chapters 1–5 experience.

## Objective
- Build a complete playable browser survival-horror game, Chapters 1–5, with the requested original world and presentation.

## Requirements
- Third-person controls, flashlight, rain, fog, monsters, ammunition, inventory, health, puzzles, locked doors, saves, cutscenes, mobile controls, and atmospheric presentation.
- Five connected chapters set in an abandoned Indian town, hospital, and police station.
- Continue the unresolved Project Eclipse story toward a future 12-chapter campaign.

## Decisions
- Built as an original Three.js browser experience with a dark cinematic UI and procedural environments.
- Used locally-written placeholder/procedural 3D assets rather than external game models.
- Implemented all five chapters as progression stages with objectives, interactions, enemies, and save checkpoints.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the main HTML shell and cinematic title/ending screens in `index.html`.
- Created the full horror HUD, inventory, pause, dialogue, mobile, and responsive styling in `styles.css`.
- Created the Three.js scene, player, camera, enemies, rain, fog, lighting, objectives, combat, chapter progression, saves, and audio in `game.js`.
- Implemented Chapters 1–5 structure and their connected narrative events.

### Active
- None. The implementation exists, but an interaction/polish verification pass remains inherently unperformed.

### Blocked
- Browser runtime verification and screenshots were not completed in the summarized work session.

## Next Move
1. Open `index.html` through a local server and run the game.
2. Verify all five chapter transitions, interactions, save/restore, and inventory/medkit behavior.
3. Test desktop and mobile input, then visually inspect the latest browser screenshot.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: Game structure, HUD, title, dialogue, and ending markup.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/styles.css`: Complete visual design and responsive/mobile styling.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js`: Three.js game implementation and all gameplay systems.

## Important Context
- Files were created directly in the workspace but a final browser build/play test was not recorded.
- Save data uses `localStorage` under the key `last-sanctuary-save`.
- The implementation uses CDN-hosted Three.js and external Google Fonts/Unsplash assets, so visual/runtime behavior may depend on network availability.

- Build a complete playable browser survival-horror game spanning Chapters 1–5, continuing the Project Eclipse story toward a future 12-chapter campaign.

## Objective
- Build a playable browser survival-horror game spanning Chapters 1–5, setting up Project Eclipse for a future 12-chapter campaign.

## Requirements
- Include third-person controls, flashlight, rain, fog, monsters, ammunition, inventory, health, puzzles, locked doors, saves, cutscenes, mobile controls, and atmospheric presentation.
- Connect the chapters across an abandoned Indian town, hospital, and police station.

## Decisions
- Use an original Three.js browser experience with procedural environments and locally written placeholder assets.
- Store saves in `localStorage` under `last-sanctuary-save`; load Three.js from jsDelivr.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the title screen, game HUD, dialogue and ending UI in `index.html` and responsive styling in `styles.css`.
- Implemented procedural scenes and characters, rain, lighting, chapter objectives, interaction, combat, inventory, health, dialogue, saves, and desktop/mobile controls in `game.js`.
- Installed Playwright Chromium and opened the game at `http://localhost:3002`.
- Verified the title screen and started the game; the Chapter 1 HUD and dialogue appeared, and browser screenshots were captured.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Finish browser gameplay verification, especially movement, interaction/objective progression, combat, inventory, checkpoint restore, chapter transitions, and mobile input.
- Investigate why movement tests only changed the displayed target distance slightly and did not reveal an interaction prompt or objective progression.

### Blocked
- No hard blocker; gameplay verification is incomplete.

## Next Move
1. Continue Playwright testing at `http://localhost:3002`, beginning with reliable movement and interaction near the Chapter 1 objective.
2. Check combat, inventory/medkits, save and restore, chapter transitions, and mobile controls; fix any issues found.
3. Review browser console output and optionally address the `favicon.ico` 404.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game structure, HUD, title, dialogue, ending, and controls.
- `game.js`: Three.js scene and gameplay systems.
- `styles.css`: Visual design and responsive/mobile styling.

## Important Context
- Game files are untracked; no commit or push was made.
- Browser rendered the game and started a new game successfully. Console showed a `favicon.ico` 404 and WebGL performance warnings; no gameplay-breaking JavaScript errors were observed.
- Chapter progression, checkpoint restore, combat, and mobile controls have not yet been verified.

## Objective
- Build a playable browser survival-horror game spanning Chapters 1–5, setting up Project Eclipse for a future 12-chapter campaign.

## Requirements
- Include third-person controls, flashlight, rain, fog, monsters, ammunition, inventory, health, puzzles, locked doors, saves, cutscenes, mobile controls, and atmospheric presentation.
- Connect the chapters across an abandoned Indian town, hospital, and police station.

## Decisions
- Use an original Three.js browser experience with procedural environments and locally written placeholder assets.
- Store saves in `localStorage` under `last-sanctuary-save`; load Three.js from jsDelivr.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the title screen, HUD, dialogue and ending UI in `index.html` and responsive styling in `styles.css`.
- Implemented procedural scenes, characters, rain, lighting, chapter objectives, interaction, combat, inventory, health, dialogue, saves, and desktop/mobile controls in `game.js`.
- Verified all five chapters can progress through their three stages and reach the ending in browser testing.
- Verified keyboard movement responds, inventory opens, and checkpoint save/continue works; `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` previously passed.

### Active
- Fix and retest objective interactions: moving near the Chapter 1 objective did not reveal the prompt or progress the objective.
- Diagnose apparent gameplay performance issue: under normal rendering the browser advanced very few animation frames; disabling `renderer.render(scene,camera);` in a temporary test made movement work, suggesting rendering/GPU load may be responsible.
- Verify combat and mobile input under actual gameplay conditions; no successful verification yet.

### Blocked
- Browser gameplay testing is unreliable with full rendering due to severe apparent frame stalls in headless Playwright; need a workable rendering/browser test setup to distinguish performance from gameplay bugs.

## Next Move
1. Inspect target position and `nearestInteractable()` behavior; investigate why prompt and interaction did not work even when close to the active target.
2. Profile/mitigate rendering load or test in a browser environment with functional WebGL; confirm animation frames, movement, and interactions without test-only source replacements.
3. Recheck combat, healing, checkpoint restore, and mobile joystick/buttons with successful gameplay input.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, gameplay systems, controls, interaction, chapter progression, and saves.
- `index.html`: Game UI, HUD, title, dialogue, ending, and mobile controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual design and responsive/mobile styling.

## Important Context
- Game files are untracked; no commit or push was made.
- Server is available at `http://localhost:3002`.
- Testing progression to the ending succeeded using a temporary Playwright route that removed rendering; that harness-only progression is not evidence that normal gameplay works.
- Normal rendering test showed movement from `[-21,0,3]` to approximately `[-14,0,3]`, but objective prompt stayed hidden and interaction did not advance stage.
- Browser console/page errors were absent in recent checks. Earlier `favicon.ico` 404 and WebGL performance warnings were observed.

## Objective
- Build a playable browser survival-horror game spanning Chapters 1–5, setting up Project Eclipse for a future 12-chapter campaign.

## Requirements
- Include third-person controls, flashlight, rain, fog, monsters, ammunition, inventory, health, puzzles, locked doors, saves, cutscenes, mobile controls, and atmospheric presentation.
- Connect the chapters across an abandoned Indian town, hospital, and police station.

## Decisions
- Use an original Three.js browser experience with procedural environments and locally written placeholder assets.
- Store saves in `localStorage` under `last-sanctuary-save`; load Three.js from jsDelivr.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the title screen, HUD, dialogue and ending UI in `index.html` and responsive styling in `styles.css`.
- Implemented procedural scenes, characters, rain, lighting, chapter objectives, interaction, combat, inventory, health, dialogue, saves, and desktop/mobile controls in `game.js`.
- Earlier progression tests reached the ending across all five chapters, but used a temporary test route that disabled rendering; this does not verify normal gameplay.
- Recently raised interaction range from `2.55` to `3.35`, moved objective spots to the clear central play lane, disabled shadows, reduced pixel ratio to `1.2`, replaced some decorative point lights, and removed a global fill point light in `game.js`.

- Retest objective prompts and interactions with the updated `objectiveSpots` and interaction range.

2. Measure frame rate after the latest rendering reductions; profile remaining expensive rendering work if performance is still poor.
3. Verify combat, healing, checkpoint restore, and mobile controls under usable gameplay conditions.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js scene, rendering settings, objectives, interaction, controls, combat, and saves.
- `index.html`: Game UI, HUD, title, dialogue, ending, and mobile controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual design and responsive/mobile styling.

## Objective
- Build a playable browser survival-horror game spanning Chapters 1–5, setting up Project Eclipse for a future 12-chapter campaign.

## Requirements
- Include third-person controls, flashlight, rain, fog, monsters, ammunition, inventory, health, puzzles, locked doors, saves, cutscenes, mobile controls, and atmospheric presentation.
- Connect the chapters across an abandoned Indian town, hospital, and police station.

## Decisions
- Use an original Three.js browser experience with procedural environments and locally written placeholder assets.
- Store saves in `localStorage` under `last-sanctuary-save`; load Three.js from jsDelivr.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the title screen, HUD, dialogue and ending UI in `index.html` and responsive styling in `styles.css`.
- Implemented procedural scenes, characters, rain, lighting, chapter objectives, interaction, combat, inventory, health, dialogue, saves, and desktop/mobile controls in `game.js`.
- Raised interaction range to `3.35` and placed objective spots in the clear central play lane.
- Confirmed browser testing with rendering disabled could progress through all five chapters; this did not verify normal gameplay.

### Active
- Repair `game.js` after the latest edits: `playerLight` and `playerLightTarget` are now set to `null`, but the animation loop and flashlight handler still dereference them. A browser probe after this change reported `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'position')` and `Cannot set properties of null (setting 'visible')`.
- Diagnose and reduce rendering cost without breaking lighting or gameplay. A temporary, request-intercepted experiment that removed point lights measured around 60 FPS in SwiftShader, but this was not applied safely to the actual game.
- Retest prompts/interactions, movement, combat, healing, checkpoint restore, and mobile input during normal rendering.

### Blocked
- Normal gameplay testing is blocked until the null-light regression is fixed.

## Next Move
1. Inspect and repair the actual light initialization and every `playerLight`, `playerLightTarget`, `muzzle`, and target-glow reference in `game.js`.
2. Run `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check`, then reload the game and confirm there are no runtime errors.
3. Profile normal rendering again; use the temporary point-light-removal result to guide safe optimizations.
4. Retest objective interaction and core gameplay systems under normal rendering.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js renderer, lighting, objectives, interaction, controls, combat, and saves.
- `index.html`: Game UI, HUD, title, dialogue, ending, and mobile controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual design and responsive/mobile styling.

## Important Context
- Game files are untracked; no commit or push was made.
- Server is available at `http://localhost:3002`.
- Playwright uses headless Chromium with SwiftShader; rendering performance measurements reflect that environment.
- Latest actual edits in `game.js` removed target glow intensity updates and set `playerLight`/`playerLightTarget` to `null` without removing their remaining uses.

## Objective
- Build a playable browser survival-horror game spanning Chapters 1–5, setting up Project Eclipse for a future 12-chapter campaign.

## Requirements
- Include third-person controls, flashlight, rain, fog, monsters, ammunition, inventory, health, puzzles, locked doors, saves, cutscenes, mobile controls, and atmospheric presentation.
- Connect the chapters across an abandoned Indian town, hospital, and police station.

## Decisions
- Use an original Three.js browser experience with procedural environments and locally written placeholder assets.
- Store saves in `localStorage` under `last-sanctuary-save`; load Three.js from jsDelivr.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the title screen, HUD, dialogue and ending UI in `index.html` and responsive styling in `styles.css`.
- Implemented procedural scenes, characters, rain, lighting, chapter objectives, interaction, combat, inventory, health, dialogue, saves, and desktop/mobile controls in `game.js`.
- Fixed the null flashlight regression: initialized a player spotlight and target; replaced muzzle flash with a visible mesh.
- Reduced point-light rendering costs by replacing environment and enemy point lights, removing target glow lights, and using emissive enemy hit feedback.
- Verified `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` pass.
- Browser-tested initialization and gameplay without runtime page errors: reached an objective, interacted to advance, advanced dialogue, opened inventory and pause UI, saved and restored a checkpoint, and confirmed mobile controls display at a mobile viewport.
- Measured about 19 FPS in headless SwiftShader during a short gameplay probe.

### Active
- Improve and profile rendering performance beyond the observed ~19 FPS.
- Exercise combat, healing, checkpoint restore details, objective progression through later chapters, and actual touch input under normal rendering.
- Investigate the browser console’s 404 resource errors; they appeared during initial and subsequent probes but were not traced.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Profile the current normal-rendering scene and reduce remaining performance bottlenecks while preserving lighting and presentation.
2. Trace the 404 resource request and fix it if it belongs to the game.
3. Retest firing, enemy damage/defeat, ammunition pickup/reload, healing, saved-stage restoration, chapter transitions, and mobile joystick/actions; record any issues.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Three.js renderer, lighting, objectives, interaction, controls, combat, and saves.
- `index.html`: Game UI, HUD, title, dialogue, ending, and mobile controls.
- `styles.css`: Visual design and responsive/mobile styling.

## Important Context
- Game files are untracked; no commit or push was made.
- Server is available at `http://localhost:3002`.
- Playwright headless Chromium with SwiftShader is available through the runtime tooling; FPS measurements reflect that environment.
